requirement.title: Staged spec-delta records support amend, retract, and full operation vocabulary
requirement.body: The change-owned staged spec-delta record (change.deltas[capability][]) supports the complete write vocabulary through public tools: adv_delta_add (add), adv_delta_modify (first modify), adv_delta_amend (replace an already-staged delta, preserving its id), adv_delta_retract (remove a staged delta), adv_delta_remove (stage an operation:remove delta), and adv_delta_rename (stage an operation:rename delta). Amend is full-replace (deterministic — the caller supplies the complete corrected delta; no heuristic merge). Every write returns explicit failure rather than false success when the post-signal readback cannot confirm the intended change (mutation-safety readback proof). Archive remains the sole global-spec writer; these tools only mutate the change-owned staged record. New signal handlers are additive and replay-safe.

scenarios.when: adv_delta_amend or adv_delta_retract is called with a deltaId that is not staged

documents.proposal:
## Problem

`change.deltas[capability][]` is the change-owned durable delta record (Delta = discriminated union on `operation`: add | modify | remove | rename — specs.ts:223). Write coverage is half-built:
- ✅ `adv_delta_add` → stages operation:add
- ✅ `adv_delta_modify` → stages operation:modify (FIRST modify of a capability-local target only; a second modify of the same target is rejected as a conflict)
- ❌ No tool to AMEND a staged delta (fix its postimage after staging)
- ❌ No tool to RETRACT a staged delta
- ❌ No tool to stage operation:remove or operation:rename — even though the types are in the union AND the downstream fully applies/validates them (archive/delta.ts:25-27 applyRemoveDelta + rename; archive/projection.ts:275; validator/conflicts.ts:99,197,463-521; validator/completeness.ts:156)

Live blocker (from the replaceRecoveryToolSprawl agent): amending a staged modify-delta on `rq-activeChangePointer01` (scenarios .1/.2/.6 → adv_change_forget→adv_doctor; preserve .3/.4/.5/.7). The requirement stays, the cross-project pointer changes stay — only the staged delta's postimage needs correcting. No tool can do this today.

## Design (research-backed: adv-researcher findings on delta CRUD, this session)

### Primary — B/amend (THE BLOCKER)
`adv_delta_amend(changeId, capability, deltaId, delta)`:
- Requires the staged delta with `deltaId` to exist under `capability`.
- **Full-replace, deterministic (P33 — no heuristic merge):** caller supplies the COMPLETE corrected delta (e.g. all scenarios .1-.7, with .1/.2/.6 updated and .3/.4/.5/.7 included unchanged). Tool atomically swaps the staged entry.
- **Preserves the delta id** (`dl-xxx` stays stable so any references hold).
- New payload validated exactly like add/modify (modify target must still exist; scenario-id parenting rules; duplicate/precondition checks).
- Readback proof (mutation-safety SC4+SC6 pattern already on trunk): success means the amended delta is durably present, else typed failure.

### B/retract (undo companion)
`adv_delta_retract(changeId, capability, deltaId)`: atomically drop the staged delta by id. Readback proof (delta absent).

### A — operation vocabulary completion (downstream already done)
`adv_delta_remove(changeId, capability, delta)` → stages operation:remove (target_id + reason).
`adv_delta_rename(changeId, capability, delta)` → stages operation:rename.
Mirror adv_delta_add/adv_delta_modify exactly. Downstream apply/projection/validate/conflict already handle both.

## Structural properties

- **No migration.** Delta union already includes remove/rename; `change.deltas[]` shape unchanged. Amend/retract mutate the array in place. No version bump, no data transform.
- **Replay-safe.** New signals (specDeltaAmended/Retracted/Removed/Renamed) are additive `wf.setHandler` blocks (workflows.ts:1538-1549 pattern). Old histories never sent them → replay never reaches the new handlers → no wf.patched() marker needed. Must pass replay-determinism tests (verification, not migration).
- **Archive remains sole global-spec writer.** These tools only mutate the change-owned staged delta record; application still happens at archive.
- **Atomic + typed reject** on unknown deltaId, invalid payload, conflicting target — mirrors existing add/modify guarantees.

## Files (mirror adv_delta_modify)
`temporal/contracts.ts` (signal names) · `temporal/messages.ts` (defineSignal) · `types/signals.ts` (payload schemas) · `temporal/workflows.ts` (setHandler + reducers: amend=replace-by-id, retract=drop-by-id, remove/rename=append) · `storage/store-temporal/spec-deltas.ts` (store methods) · `tools/spec-delta.ts` (4 tools) · `tool-registry.ts` + `tool-role-policy.ts` (register) · tests · schemas:generate + generate:manifests · spec delta for the new capability law.

## Coordination (no agent stop/restart)
Worktree isolation — build in a separate change worktree; do NOT interrupt the replaceRecoveryToolSprawl agent. Merge-time only: `workflows.ts` / `tool-registry.ts` / `tool-role-policy.ts` overlap is ADDITIVE (adjacent new entries) → mechanical conflicts, 2nd-merged rebases (auto via #288) + reruns build:worker + replay-determinism before deploy. Deploy from merged trunk, never a worktree. This change UNBLOCKS that agent, so land it first if possible.

## Out of scope
- Changing how deltas apply at archive (downstream unchanged).
- Cross-project delta semantics.
- Merge/patch-style partial amend (deliberately full-replace for determinism).
documents.problemStatement: The change-owned spec-delta record supports only two write operations: adv_delta_add (operation:add) and adv_delta_modify (operation:modify, first modification only). There is no public tool to (1) AMEND a delta already staged on an active change — adv_delta_modify allows the first modify of a requirement but rejects a second modify of the same capability-local target, so an agent who staged a modify cannot later correct its postimage; (2) RETRACT a staged delta; or (3) stage remove/rename OPERATION deltas — despite DeltaRemoveSchema/DeltaRenameSchema existing in the Delta discriminated union (specs.ts:198-226) and the entire downstream (archive/delta.ts applyRemoveDelta, archive/projection.ts, validator/conflicts.ts, validator/completeness.ts) already fully handling remove and rename. Concrete live blocker: an agent updating rq-activeChangePointer01 to replace retired-tool references (adv_change_forget → adv_doctor) across scenarios .1/.2/.6 while preserving .3/.4/.5/.7 staged the modify, then could not amend it.
documents.agreement:
## Objectives
1. An agent can amend a spec-delta already staged on an active change, correcting its postimage, without removing the requirement or losing prior staged content.
2. An agent can retract (unstage) a delta from an active change.
3. An agent can stage remove and rename operation deltas (completing the write path for operations the downstream already applies).

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1 (amend): Given a modify-delta staged under a capability, when `adv_delta_amend(changeId, capability, deltaId, delta)` is called with a complete corrected delta, then the staged entry is atomically replaced, the delta id is preserved, and `adv_change_show` exposes the amended postimage before success is returned; a second amend of the same delta succeeds (no first-modify-only limit).
- AC2 (amend validation): Given an amend whose new payload is invalid (unknown modify target, bad scenario-id parenting, malformed), when called, then the operation is atomically rejected and the previously-staged delta is unchanged.
- AC3 (retract): Given a staged delta, when `adv_delta_retract(changeId, capability, deltaId)` is called, then the delta is removed from the change record and `adv_change_show` no longer lists it; readback confirms absence before success.
- AC4 (remove op): Given a valid remove delta (target_id + reason), when `adv_delta_remove` is called, then operation:remove is staged, readback-confirmed, and archive simulation applies it via the existing applyRemoveDelta path.
- AC5 (rename op): Given a valid rename delta, when `adv_delta_rename` is called, then operation:rename is staged and readback-confirmed.
- AC6 (unknown id): Given a deltaId that is not staged, when amend or retract is called, then a typed not-found error is returned with no mutation.
- AC7 (persistence proof): Every new tool returns explicit failure (not false success) when the signal is acknowledged but the post-signal readback cannot confirm the intended change (mutation-safety SC4+SC6).
- AC8 (no regression): adv_delta_add and adv_delta_modify behavior is unchanged; full targeted delta suite passes.
- AC9 (replay determinism): New signal handlers are additive; replay-determinism tests pass; no wf.patched() marker required and none added.

## Constraints
- C1: Archive remains the sole global-spec writer; these tools only mutate the change-owned staged delta record.
- C2: No migration — the Delta discriminated union already includes remove/rename; change.deltas[] shape is unchanged.
- C3: Amend is full-replace (deterministic, P33) — caller supplies the complete corrected delta; no heuristic merge.
- C4: New signals are additive and replay-safe; must not alter existing signal-handler ordering.
- C5: Preserve add-only-friendly guarantees: atomic reject on unknown id / invalid payload / conflicting target.

## Avoidances
- DONT1: Do not add a partial/patch merge mode for amend.
- DONT2: Do not change how deltas apply at archive.
- DONT3: Do not touch cross-project delta semantics.
- DONT4: Do not interrupt or restart the replaceRecoveryToolSprawl agent; coordinate at merge only.
- DONT5: Do not add wf.patched() markers or reorder existing signal handlers.
documents.design:
## Architecture

Mirror the existing `adv_delta_modify` write path four ways. Each new tool: validate → `fireSignalWithMutationGuard` (SC4+SC6) → post-signal readback proof → persist. No new persistence, no migration.

## Signals (temporal/contracts.ts + messages.ts)
- `specDeltaAmended` — payload { capability, deltaId, delta } (full replacement)
- `specDeltaRetracted` — payload { capability, deltaId }
- `specDeltaRemoved` — payload { capability, delta: DeltaRemove }
- `specDeltaRenamed` — payload { capability, delta: DeltaRename }

## Reducers (temporal/workflows.ts, additive setHandler blocks; types/change-state.ts appliers)
- amend: find staged delta by `deltaId` under capability → replace in place, PRESERVE id → reject if absent or new payload invalid.
- retract: find by `deltaId` → drop from array → reject if absent.
- remove/rename: append (mirror add/modify), reject duplicate id / conflicting target.
All reducers append typed `signal_rejections` on failure (existing pattern) so the store readback surfaces a typed error.

## Store (storage/store-temporal/spec-deltas.ts)
Four methods mirroring `.modify`: fire guarded signal → classify readback → query state → find (amend/remove/rename: entry present with expected op; retract: entry ABSENT) → throw typed error on mismatch → setCached/emitSummary/persistToDisk → return.

## Tools (tools/spec-delta.ts)
- `adv_delta_amend(changeId, capability, deltaId, delta)` — full-replace; delta validated as a complete Delta (add/modify/remove/rename) matching the staged entry's operation; modify keeps DeltaModify scenario-parenting rules.
- `adv_delta_retract(changeId, capability, deltaId)`
- `adv_delta_remove(changeId, capability, delta)` — DeltaRemove
- `adv_delta_rename(changeId, capability, delta)` — DeltaRename
Registered in tool-registry.ts; policy entries in tool-role-policy.ts (same realm/group as adv_delta_add/modify).

## Determinism (AC9)
New signals = new handlers appended after existing ones. Old histories never sent them → replay never enters them. No `wf.patched()` (DONT5). Verify via replay-determinism.test.ts.

## Amend semantics (AC1/C3)
Full-replace: caller sends the COMPLETE corrected delta. For the live case (rq-activeChangePointer01), caller resends all scenarios .1-.7 with .1/.2/.6 corrected and .3/.4/.5/.7 unchanged; tool swaps the staged entry, keeps `dl-xxx`. Deterministic, no merge heuristic.

## Spec law
Add a requirement to advance-workflow capability covering amend/retract/remove/rename staged-delta write semantics + readback proof (staged via this change's own delta record).

## Validator note
No user-value tradeoff or contract-compromise; straight feature-completion of an existing, downstream-ready vocabulary. Independent validation not required beyond replay-determinism + targeted suite.
documents.executiveSummary:
## Outcome

Agents can now correct staged spec-deltas mid-change. Four new tools complete the staged-delta write vocabulary: `adv_delta_amend` (full-replace a staged delta, preserving its id — the primary unblock), `adv_delta_retract` (drop a staged delta), and `adv_delta_remove` / `adv_delta_rename` (stage remove/rename operations the downstream already applied).

## Why It Matters

`adv_delta_modify` allowed only a *first* modify of a requirement and rejected any later correction — an agent who staged a wrong postimage was stuck (cancel + recreate the change was the only escape). This directly unblocked the replaceRecoveryToolSprawl agent, who needed to amend a staged modify on `rq-activeChangePointer01` (replacing retired-tool references adv_change_forget→adv_doctor across scenarios .1/.2/.6 while preserving .3/.4/.5/.7).

## Verification

- 90 targeted delta tests + 13 replay-determinism tests (including replay of poisoned production histories) pass
- `pnpm run check` green (schemas/typecheck/manifests/lint/format); `build:worker` clean
- Live post-deploy dogfood: this change's own spec-law delta `rq-stagedDeltaCrud01` round-tripped cleanly (readback-confirmed), and the workflow self-recovered via the OrphanQueueAdopter — both this session's own mechanisms validated in production

## Structural properties

- No migration — the Delta discriminated union already included remove/rename; `change.deltas[]` shape unchanged
- Replay-safe — new signal handlers appended additively; old histories never sent them; no `wf.patched()`
- Archive remains the sole global-spec writer; tools mutate only the change-owned staged record
- Full-replace amend (deterministic, no heuristic merge); every write returns explicit failure on unconfirmed readback (SC4+SC6)

## Risks / Follow-ups

- Merge coordination: additive overlap with in-flight replaceRecoveryToolSprawl on workflows.ts/tool-registry.ts/tool-role-policy.ts — that change rebases + reruns build:worker when it merges
- Sub-agent test runIds were not durably recorded (verification_missing warnings) — dispositioned with the orchestrator-run 90+13 test evidence
